Commentary.Commentary: We are back for India's second innings. The umpires are back out in the middle and the pair of skipper, Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal is all set to open the innings for India. Taskin Ahmed has the new ball in hand and will get proceedings underway for Bangladesh. Let's go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Right then, India have the lead and have plenty of time to really frustrate out there in the field. Conditions are hot and the pitch looks pristine to bat on. Bangladesh will need something really special from their frontline pacers to save face here. Join us in a bit for India's second innings or it could be Bangladesh's as well if India do decide to give the follow-on which is unlikely.

Bangladesh will be kicking themselves with that batting performance and yes, they have come back from the brink very recently against Pakistan but conceding a first-innings lead of 200-plus runs against India at home is like axing your own foot. Only four batters could even break into the 20s with Shakib Al Hasan top-scoring at 32. Mehidy Hasan looked the most settled batter as he remained unbeaten on 27 and Bangladesh failed to even play out 50 overs.

A job well done for India with the ball and they have cleaned up Bangladesh for just 149 runs, amassing a huge first-innings lead of 227 runs. They have the option of the follow-on but most likely, India will bat again and will look to make the most of what looks like pretty good batting conditions. Jasprit Bumrah starred with his four wickets with the likes of Mohammed Siraj, Akash Deep and Ravindra Jadeja all picking a couple of wickets each. Ravichandran Ashwin was the only bowler not to pick up a wicket, rarely does that happen here in Chennai.

... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Right then, the Bangladeshi tail has it all do it and it is a huge ask for them to even get out of follow-on territory but not impossible and the pitch looks more than decent for batting as well. India will look to attack early after Tea and bundle out the visitors. Join us in a few minutes' time at 9 am GMT for the final session on Day 2.

India began the second session on Day 2 well and have now closed it out pretty solidly as well. After Lunch, Mohammed Siraj and Jasprit Bumrah bowled small but fiery spells and picked up a wicket each. However, India soon reverted to spin as the shine on the ball was lost and there was hardly any lateral movement on a flattening pitch. The duo of Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja remained fairly tight and finally, it was Jadeja who won the battle of patience against the two set batters. Bumrah was given the final over before Tea and he delivered yet again with a wicket.

Bangladesh came into the post-Lunch session, rattled by Akash Deep in the final over before Lunch and needed to just see off the pacers for a bit which didn't happen. Najmul Hossain Shanto who looked solid was the first one to fall before Bangladesh's crisis man, Mushfiqur Rahim too fell. Then came the stand between Shakib Al Hasan and Litton Das worth 51 runs but soon enough, a couple of unnecessary sweep shots from both batters when the ball was hardly turning brought about their demise, leaving the visitors reeling. They lost their 8th wicket on the stroke of Tea and have been blown away here.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27.5 overs, 86 runs and 5 wickets! Another excellent session for India in the field and at Tea on Day 2, the hosts are in complete control of the Test match. Bangladesh on the other hand have had a torrid time with the bat and still need 65 more runs to avoid the follow-on. Anything less than that and India can ask them to bat again if they want to.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back, folks! The post-Lunch session is just about to begin. The umpires are punctual and are out to the middle. Indian players are circled in a team huddle before spreading out to their respective fielding positions. Najmul Hossain Shanto will take the strike and will be accompanied by the Bangladeshi veteran Mushfiqur Rahim. Mohammed Siraj (3-1-6-0) will kick off the proceedings with the ball for India. And, here we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, India has firmly got a grip in this match as of now as they have a very healthy lead of 350 runs. Bangladesh struggled with the bat initially and it will be interesting to see how they negotiate against the spin. Although the second session is considered the best time to bat on, and with extremely sunny conditions out there, the Bangladeshi batters will aim to make an impactful comeback. An interesting second session awaits us which will begin at 6.40 am GMT. Stay tuned.

Bangladesh then stepped up to the crease with the bat, hoping to get off to a strong positive start. But those hopes were quickly dashed when Jasprit Bumrah threw a wrench in their plans right from the first over. Bumrah got rid of Shadman Islam off an absolute seed that left him bamboozled. From the word go, Bumrah and Siraj formed a threatening tandem and interrogated with some peach of deliveries. But the trouble didn't end there, Akash Deep was introduced into the attack and he too, made an immediate impact with a couple of wickets right on the cusp of Lunch which left Bangladesh in an absolute distraught.

Bangladesh, having endured an unexpected challenge towards the end of Day 1, returned to the field with renewed vigour. Armed with the new ball, their bowling attack showed marked improvement. Taskin Ahmed, who had struggled to find his rhythm on the opening day, bounced back impressively. He exhibited better control over his line and length, resulting in a brilliant three-wicket haul. The highlight of the bowling performance, however, was Hasan Mahmud. After coming tantalisingly close, he finally secured his fifth wicket, etching his name in the record books as the first Bangladeshi bowler to claim a five-wicket haul on Indian soil.

Chepauk's contrasting weather from the previous day, a characteristically sunny, warm, and humid environment greeted the players on Day 2. The conditions were typically conducive to batting. However, contrary to expectations, India's innings took a dramatic turn. Despite a decent start from the overnight batters, the situation rapidly deteriorated. Within a span of just a few overs, India lost both the well-set Jadeja and Ashwin and the 199-run stand for the seventh wicket was broken, followed by a swift dismissal of the tail-enders. Akash Deep's late cameo with the bat helped India reach a final total of 376.
